label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
Kavya, I’ve been thinking about your post. I don’t want to turn this into a public argument, especially because I respect you and the friendship we’ve built in Foundry91 Cohort 4.

You sat with me until 1 a.m. in the Koramangala office, helping untangle DabbaDost’s Razorpay webhook mess before demo day in March. I’ve never forgotten that. So I’m sorry this has become a source of hurt between us.

I also want to clear up a couple of things, because the details matter. We posted a backend developer opening on LinkedIn and Instahyre on 14 September, open to anyone. One person applied on 19 September; the second came through a referral about two weeks later. Nobody from my side DM’d anyone. Both offers were 22% above their existing CTC, not 40%, and both people joined us on 3 November.

On ESOPs: DabbaDost does have an ESOP pool. It’s small, but it’s real and has been on paper since January. We didn’t promise something we don’t have.

But I should have handled this better. I knew from the start where the applicants worked. I should have called you before making the offers, not after the second one was accepted. I WhatsApped you then, and when I didn’t hear back, I should still have picked up the phone. I’m sorry I didn’t.

This isn’t about blaming anyone, and I don’t want the people involved pulled into a public conversation. In a cohort of 11 startups hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala, this will happen again. We need a better way to handle it.

Could we agree on a simple cohort rule: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer? Not to ask permission—just to keep communication respectful and avoid surprises.

Kavya, I’m saying this publicly because the conversation is public, not because I want a fight. I respect you, and I’d rather talk this through than trade posts. Coffee or a call this week, whenever you’re comfortable. My door’s open.
